169.stem:
In a reducing-balance loan, an amount $\text{\textdollar}P$ is borrowed for a period of $n$ months at an interest rate of $0.25\%$ per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of $\text{\textdollar}M$ is made. After the $n$th repayment has been made, the amount owing, $\text{\textdollar}A_n$, is given by

$$A_n=P(1.0025)^n-M\left(1+(1.0025)^1+(1.0025)^2+\cdots+(1.0025)^{n-1}\right).$$

(Do NOT prove this.)

parts.latex:
Jane borrows $\text{\textdollar}200\,000$ in a reducing-balance loan as described.

The loan is to be repaid in 180 monthly repayments.

Show that $M=1381.16$, when rounded to the nearest cent.

After 100 repayments of $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$ have been made, the interest rate changes to $0.35\%$ per month.

At this stage, the amount owing to the nearest dollar is $\text{\textdollar}100\,032$. (Do NOT prove this.)

Jane continues to make the same monthly repayments.

For how many more months will Jane need to make full monthly payments of $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$?

The final repayment will be less than $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$.

How much will Jane need to pay in the final payment in order to pay off the loan?

criteria: Uses the sum for a geometric progression
Writes the equation in simplest exponential form
Writes the equation in terms of $n$ using the new interest rate and the new principal

solutions.latex:
After 83 payments,
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount owing} &= 100\,032(1.0035)^{83} - 1381.16\left[\dfrac{(1.0035)^{83} - 1}{1.0035 - 1}\right] \\ &= 928.29 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Final payment (84th month)} &= 928.29 \times 1.0035 \quad \text{(1-month interest)} \\ &= 931.54 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes $n = 83$ into amount owing, or equivalent merit

Geometric series.reason: Uses the A_n formula already established in part (b); no GP summation done here

solutions.latex:
She needs to repay for $n$ more months:
$$\begin{aligned} 350000(1.005)^n - 2998\left(\dfrac{1.005^n - 1}{0.005}\right) &= 0 \\ 350000(1.005)^n - 2998\times 200\left(1.005^n - 1\right) &= 0 \\ (350000 - 2998\times 200)\,1.005^n &= -2998\times 200 \\ 1.005^n &= \dfrac{1499}{624} \\ n &= \log_{1.005}\left(\dfrac{1499}{624}\right) \\ n &= 175.72 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ The loan is repaid after $176$ more months.
criteria: Forms the equation $A_n=0$ with $350000$ and $2998$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
When $n = 175$:
$$350000(1.005)^{175} - 2998\times 200\left(1.005^{175} - 1\right) = 2144.74\ldots$$
After one month, the last repayment is
$$2144.74\times 1.005 = 2155.46\ldots \approx \$2156$$
Method 2: when $n = 176$:
$$350000(1.005)^{176} - 2998\times 200\left(1.005^{176} - 1\right) \approx -842.54$$
$$2998 + (-842.54) \approx \$2156$$
$\therefore$ The last repayment is $\$2156$.
criteria: Finds the amount owing after $175$ repayments ($2144.74$) or $A_{176}\approx-842.54$, or equivalent merit

513.stem:
A borrower obtains a reducing-balance loan of $\$800\,000$ to buy a house.

Interest is charged at $0.5\%$ monthly, compounded monthly.

On the last day of each month, interest is added to the balance owing on the loan and then the monthly repayment of $\$5740$ is made.

Let $\$A_n$ be the balance owing on the loan at the end of $n$ months.

parts.latex: After how many months will the balance owing on the loan first be less than $\$400\,000$?

criteria: Provides a correct $A_1$, or equivalent merit
Uses the sum of a geometric sequence in $A_n$, or equivalent merit
Provides an expression that shows evidence of the pattern, or equivalent merit
Attempts to use logarithms to find $n$, or equivalent merit

560.stem:
Peyton borrows \$83 000. Any amount owing on the loan attracts interest at an annual rate of $6\%$, compounded monthly.

The repayments are made at the end of each month after the interest is added to the account.

Peyton makes a first monthly repayment of \$760 and then increases the value of the repayment by $10\%$ each month.

Let $A_n$ = Amount owing after the $n$th repayment.

parts.latex: Find the amount of the final payment.

criteria: Finds correct expressions for $A_1$ and $A_2$, or equivalent merit

meta.check: Simulated the loan month by month; A_3 matches the formula.

criteria: Sums the geometric series correctly, or equivalent merit
Writes the general expression for $A_n$ with the geometric series, or equivalent merit

meta.check: Closed form matches month-by-month simulation for n=1..26.

solutions.latex:
The loan is repaid when $A_n\le0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 91\,000(1.005)^n&\le8000(1.1)^n\\ \left(\dfrac{1.1}{1.005}\right)^n&\ge\dfrac{91}{8}\\ n&\ge\dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{91}{8}\right)}{\ln\left(\frac{1.1}{1.005}\right)}\approx26.9\end{aligned}$$
So $A_{26}>0$ and $A_{27}<0$: the final payment is the $27$th, and it is smaller than the scheduled $760(1.1)^{26}$.
$$\begin{aligned} A_{26}&=91\,000(1.005)^{26}-8000(1.1)^{26}\\ &\approx8254.41\end{aligned}$$
The final payment clears $A_{26}$ plus one month's interest:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{final payment}&=A_{26}\times1.005\\ &\approx\$8295.68\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds that the $27$th payment is the last and evaluates $A_{26}$, or equivalent merit
Solves $A_n=0$ (or tests values of $n$) to find $26<n<27$, or equivalent merit

meta.check: Simulated loan: after 26 payments owing 8254.41; 27th payment = 8254.41 x 1.005 = 8295.68; consistent with A_27 = -762.14.
meta.concern: Assumes the final payment is the reduced amount that clears the loan (A_26 with interest). An answer of A_26 = $8254.41 (forgetting interest) or 760(1.1)^26 = $9057.81 (full scheduled payment) is possible if NESA reads it differently.

657.stem: Ella borrows \$820 000 to purchase a house. She is being charged $8.4\%$ per annum and plans to making equal monthly repayments of \$6248 over 30 years.

parts.latex: Show that the amount owing after 10 years is \$724 960.57

After paying the home loan off for 10 years, Ella gets a pay rise. Immediately after making the 120$^{\text{th}}$ payment, Ella makes a one-off payment to reduce the balance owing to \$720 000. She then increases her monthly repayments so that the loan is paid off 25 years after the initial loan. Calculate the amount of her new monthly payment.

criteria: Writes an expression for $A_{120}$, or equivalent merit
Establishes a pattern and writes an expression for $A_2$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
After the one-off payment the balance is $\$720\,000$. The loan is paid off 25 years after it began, so $25-10=15$ years, or $180$ months, remain. Let $M$ be the new monthly repayment.

After $n$ more months the amount owing is
$$A_n=1.007^n\times 720000-M-M\times 1.007-M\times 1.007^2-\ldots-M\times 1.007^{n-1}$$
The repayments form a GP with first term $M$ and ratio $1.007$, and the loan is repaid when $A_{180}=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=1.007^{180}\times 720000-\dfrac{M(1.007^{180}-1)}{1.007-1}\\0&=1.007^{180}\times 720000-\dfrac{M(1.007^{180}-1)}{0.007}\\1.007^{180}\times 720000&=\dfrac{M(1.007^{180}-1)}{0.007}\\1.007^{180}\times 720000\times 0.007&=M(1.007^{180}-1)\\M&=\dfrac{1.007^{180}\times 720000\times 0.007}{1.007^{180}-1}\\&=7047.983754\\&=\$7047.98\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes an expression to find the monthly repayment, or equivalent merit

583.stem: Alex takes out a loan at an interest rate of $5\%$ per annum, compounded annually. At the end of each year, interest is charged and then Alex makes a repayment.

parts.latex: Suppose Alex borrows $\$10\,000$ and he pays off the loan in $10$ years with regular annual repayments of $\$M$. Let $A_n$ be the amount Alex still owes by the end of the $n^{\text{th}}$ year.
Find $A_1$ and hence $A_2$ in terms of $M$.
Find $A_n$ in terms of $M$ and $n$.
Find $M$ correct to two decimal places.

Geometric series.evidence: Sums the geometric series to obtain A_n=10000(1.05)^n−M×(1.05^n−1)/0.05

parts.latex: If Alex only wants to repay $\$350$ each year in order to pay off his loan in $20$ years, what is the maximum amount he would be able to borrow under the same interest rate? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

Geometric series.evidence: B = 20(350)(1.05^20 - 1)/1.05^20 (GP sum inside the loan formula)

solutions.latex:
Each year interest is added (multiply by $1.05$) and then $M$ is repaid:
$$A_1=10000(1.05)-M$$
$$\begin{aligned} A_2&=A_1(1.05)-M \\ &=\left[10000(1.05)-M\right](1.05)-M \\ &=10000(1.05)^2-M(1.05)-M \end{aligned}$$

Continuing the pattern from part (i):
$$\begin{aligned} A_2&=10000(1.05)^2-M(1+1.05) \\ A_n&=10000(1.05)^n-M\left(1+1.05+1.05^2+\cdots+1.05^{n-1}\right) \end{aligned}$$

The bracket is a geometric series with $a=1$, $r=1.05$, $n$ terms:
$$\begin{aligned} A_n&=10000(1.05)^n-M\times\dfrac{1.05^n-1}{0.05} \\ &=10000(1.05)^n-20M(1.05^n-1) \end{aligned}$$
The loan is repaid after $10$ years, so $A_{10}=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0&=10000(1.05)^{10}-20M(1.05^{10}-1) \\ M&=\dfrac{10000(1.05)^{10}}{20(1.05^{10}-1)} \\ &=\$1295.05 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Sums the geometric series to obtain $A_n=10000(1.05)^n-M\times\dfrac{1.05^n-1}{0.05}$, or equivalent merit

1273.stem:
Arjun borrows \$1,000,000 for a period of 10 years at an interest rate of 0.5% per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of \$$M$ is made.

Let \$$A_n$ be the amount owing after the $n^{th}$ repayment has been made.

parts.latex: Hence show that the monthly instalment $M$ is given by: $M=\dfrac{5000(1.005)^{120}}{1.005^{120}-1}$.
Find the amount still owing to the bank after 5 years, correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
$r=0.5\%$ per month. Each month interest is added and then $M$ is repaid:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=1000000\times1.005-M\\A_2&=A_1\times1.005-M\\&=(1000000\times1.005-M)\times1.005-M\\&=1000000\times1.005^2-M\times1.005-M\end{aligned}$$

Continuing the pattern, the bracket is a GP with $a=1$, $r=1.005$ and $n$ terms, summed with $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_2&=1000000\times1.005^2-M\times1.005-M\\&\;\;\vdots\\A_n&=1000000\times1.005^n-M\times1.005^{n-1}-M\times1.005^{n-2}-\dots-M\\&=1000000\times1.005^n-M(1.005^{n-1}+1.005^{n-2}+\dots+1)\\&=1000000\times1.005^n-M\times\dfrac{1.005^n-1}{1.005-1}\\&=1000000\times1.005^n-200M(1.005^n-1)\\&=(1000000-200M)\times1.005^n+200M\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substantially progresses towards the correct solution, or obtains $A_n$ with a GP, or equivalent merit
Obtains the correct $M=11102.05$, or equivalent merit

1301.stem:
A car dealership has a car for sale for a cash price of \$20 000. It can also be bought on terms over three years. The first six months are interest free. After the first six months, reducible interest is charged at the rate of 1\% per month, calculated at the end of each month.

Repayments are to be made in equal monthly instalments beginning at the end of the first month.

A customer buys the car on these terms and agrees to monthly repayments of $\$M$. Let $\$A_n$ be the amount owing at the end of the $n^{\text{th}}$ month.

parts.latex: Find an expression for $A_6$.
Find the value of $M$.

solutions.latex:
No interest is charged in the first six months, so each month the balance falls by $M$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=20\,000-M\\A_2&=20\,000-2M\\&\ \ \vdots\\A_6&=20\,000-6M\end{aligned}$$

From month 7, interest of $1\%$ is added each month before the repayment:
$$\begin{aligned}A_7&=A_6(1.01)-M\\&=(20\,000-6M)(1.01)-M\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_8&=A_7(1.01)-M\\&=\big[(20\,000-6M)(1.01)-M\big](1.01)-M\\&=(20\,000-6M)(1.01)^2-M(1.01)-M\\&=(20\,000-6M)(1.01)^2-M(1+1.01)\end{aligned}$$

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the guideline wrote A_8 = A_2(1.01) - M; it should be A_7.

criteria: Expresses $A_{36}$ using the sum of a GP, or equivalent merit
Attempts to solve $A_{36}=0$, or equivalent merit

1338.stem: Calvin borrows \$470 000 to purchase a property at 7.1% p.a. where interest is compounded monthly. He makes repayments of \$3300 per month. Interest is calculated just before each payment.

parts.latex: Find the amount owing after the first 2 years.
Find the number of months required to repay the loan.

Recurrence relations for loans and annui.reason: A_n is taken ready-made from part (a); no balances A1, A2... are built here.

solutions.latex:
The monthly interest rate:
$$\begin{aligned}r&=7.1\%\text{ p.a.}\\ &=\dfrac{7.1}{12}\%\text{ per month}\\ &=\dfrac{71}{12\,000}\text{ per month}\end{aligned}$$
Each month interest is added to the amount owing, then the $\$3300$ repayment is subtracted:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=470\,000\left(1+\dfrac{71}{12\,000}\right)^1-3300\\ &=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\\ A_2&=A_1\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\\ &=\left[470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\right]\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\\ &=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^2-3300\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\\ &=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^2-3300\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}+1\right)\\ A_3&=A_2\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)-3300\\ &=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^3-3300\left(\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^2+\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}+1\right)\\ &\ \ \vdots\\ A_n&=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-3300\left(1+\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}+\cdots+\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^{n-1}\right)\end{aligned}$$
The bracket is a geometric series with $a=1$ and $r=\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}$, so by $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$A_n=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-\dfrac{3300\left(\left(\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-1\right)}{\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}-1}$$
After 2 years, $n=24$ months:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{24}&=470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^{24}-\dfrac{3300\left(\left(\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^{24}-1\right)}{\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}-1}\\ &=456\,654.2456\\ &=\$456\,654.25\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ $\$456\,654.25$ is still owing after 2 years.
criteria: Finds an expression for $A_1$ using exact values, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The loan is repaid when $A_n=0$. Using $A_n$ from part (a):
$$\begin{aligned}470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-\dfrac{3300\left(\left(\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-1\right)}{\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}-1}&=0\\ 470\,000\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n\times\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}-1\right)&=3300\left(\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-1\right)\\ \dfrac{16\,685}{6}\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n&=3300\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n-3300\\ -\dfrac{3115}{6}\left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n&=-3300\\ \left(\dfrac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)^n&=\dfrac{3960}{623}\\ n&=\dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{3960}{623}\right)}{\ln\left(\frac{12\,071}{12\,000}\right)}\\ &=313.50738\ldots\end{aligned}$$
The loan is not repaid after 313 months, so round up:
$$\begin{aligned}\therefore n&=314\text{ months}\\ &=26\text{ years }2\text{ months}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Collects terms with power $n$ together, or equivalent merit
